edges.description: PHOX2B governs autonomic neuronal development, and the tumours that arise are of that lineage. The intervening steps are not established in the sources cited here.
The disturbed lineage gives rise to tumours across the neuroblastic spectrum.

nodes.description: The tumours arising in PHOX2B carriers are of the sympathetic nervous system lineage, and are predominantly differentiated: ganglioneuroma and ganglioneuroblastoma more often than neuroblastoma. That skew towards maturation is the clearest clue that what the variant disturbs is the differentiation programme of autonomic neuroblasts rather than proliferation alone. The entry does not claim more than that, because no cited source establishes the mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Oncologic Phenotype of Peripheral Neuroblastic Tumors Associated With PHOX2B Non-Polyalanine Repeat Expansion Mutations.
evidence.snippet: Four tumours were "poorly differentiated," and nine were differentiated, including five ganglioneuromas, three ganglioneuroblastomas, and one differentiating neuroblastoma, hence illustrating that PHOX2B NPARM are predominantly associated with differentiating tumors.

nodes.description: A heterozygous germline variant in PHOX2B, the paired-like homeobox gene that is the master regulator of autonomic nervous system development. Two variant classes behave differently: polyalanine repeat expansions, and non-polyalanine repeat missense, frameshift or truncating variants. The difference in tumour risk between them is roughly thirty-fold, which is the central fact of this predisposition.

evidence.reference_title: Germline mutations of the paired-like homeobox 2B (PHOX2B) gene in neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: PHOX2B, therefore, stands as the first gene for which germline mutations predispose to NB.

nodes.description: Neuroblastoma, ganglioneuroblastoma or ganglioneuroma. The risk depends strongly on variant class: about 45 per cent for non-polyalanine repeat mutations against about 1 to 2 per cent for polyalanine expansions. In the original series the counts were 6 of 13 patients with a missense or frameshift variant against 2 of 161 with an in-frame expansion. Against a general-population neuroblastoma incidence of about 1 in 10,000, even the low-risk class is raised.

evidence.reference_title: Retinoblastoma and Neuroblastoma Predisposition and Surveillance.
evidence.snippet: The risk for a neural crest tumor for individuals with NPARMs is about 45%, whereas the risk for individuals with PARMs is about 1% to 2%, and essentially all of those with tumors had large PARMs (30-33 repeats; ref. 84).

evidence.reference_title: PHOX2B genotype allows for prediction of tumor risk in congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Indeed, an invasive tumor (neuroblastoma) was diagnosed in 6 (46%) of 13 patients harboring either a missense or a frameshift mutation, whereas a differentiated tumor (ganglioneuroma) was diagnosed in only 2 (1.24%) of 161 patients harboring an in-frame duplication leading to an expansion of +9 alanines in one and +13 in the other.

evidence.reference_title: Germline mutations of the paired-like homeobox 2B (PHOX2B) gene in neuroblastoma.
evidence.snippet: patients with CCHS have a high predisposing risk of developing a tumor of the sympathetic nervous system (i.e., 5%-10% occurrence of NB, ganglioneuroblastoma, and ganglioneuroma-versus 1/10,000 in the general population) (Rohrer et al. 2002).

evidence.reference_title: Oncologic Phenotype of Peripheral Neuroblastic Tumors Associated With PHOX2B Non-Polyalanine Repeat Expansion Mutations.
evidence.snippet: Nevertheless, three patients had stage 4 and one patient had stage 3 disease. Segmental chromosomal alterations, correlating with poor prognosis, were found in all the six tumors analyzed by array-comparative genomic hybridization.

evidence.reference_title: Oncologic Phenotype of Peripheral Neuroblastic Tumors Associated With PHOX2B Non-Polyalanine Repeat Expansion Mutations.
evidence.snippet: However, this tumor predisposition syndrome may also be associated with poorly differentiated tumors with unfavorable genomic profiles and clinically aggressive behaviors. The intrafamilial variability and the unpredictable tumor prognosis should be considered in genetic counseling.

meta.association: Germline PHOX2B variant, neuroblastic tumour predisposition

evidence.reference_title: PHOX2B genotype allows for prediction of tumor risk in congenital central hypoventilation syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Although modifier genes in both LO-CHS and Haddad syndrome are likely, PHOX2B is the major disease-causing gene in CCHS and is a predisposing gene to neuroblastoma whenever the mutation does not result in a polyalanine expansion.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic susceptibility to neuroblastoma: current knowledge and future directions.
evidence.snippet: PHOX2B-driven disease displays a robust genotype-phenotype association: while 45% of individuals with non-polyalanine repeat mutations (primarily missense mutations) develop neural crest tumors, only 1-2% of those with PHOX2B polyalanine expansions will develop neuroblastoma
